title: Internal JWT claims (C2)
description: Payload of the ES256 JWT issued by the gateway for MCP servers and the credential broker. Rules that a schema cannot express and that receivers MUST check: kid not starting with 'test-' unless the receiver is explicitly configured with allowTestKeys=true (unit tests and dev, CC-044), and kid not starting with 'dev-' unless the receiver is in dev mode, that is the devstack profile and allowTestKeys=true together (CC-137; allowTestKeys alone is not enough for dev-), signature against the gateway JWKS, iss, aud == own id, exp with clock skew <= 30 s, iat not more than 30 s in the future, exp - iat <= 60 s, jti not seen within its validity window (one-time, for every purpose), rid == X-Request-Id header, purpose: `use` == the purpose of the endpoint, otherwise the token is refused as wrong_purpose (CC-249): `policy-data` only for POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data of a server (C14), only in the service variant; `call` for everything else (the MCP endpoint of a server, every endpoint of the credential broker) and never for that path; GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest takes no token at all (CC-249); tool present and == params.name for tools/call, tool present for the broker resolve and for the authenticator calls of the gateway (GET /v1/authenticator, POST /v1/authenticator/verify, POST /v1/authenticator/invalidate-codes; CC-092, CC-128), tool absent for every other request (CC-038), resource (CC-260) present and == params.uri for resources/read and for the broker resolve that serves it, absent for every other request, never together with tool (the broker resolve carries exactly one of the two), pty and act (CC-260) absent for a human, pty agent without act, pty delegated with act, service variant only for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, ping, POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data and (broker) GET /v1/systems, and only outside a session (stateless, CC-070): notifications/*, GET/DELETE on the MCP endpoint, subscriptions/listen and every other request of a session carry the user variant without tool. A tools/call retry with inputResponses (MRTR, MCP 2026-07-28) is an ordinary tools/call with a fresh token (CC-069). mcp_risk and mcp_action (CC-226) only when the receiver is the sidecar of an adapter, otherwise invalid_claims. Any failure -> HTTP 401.

Header.description: JOSE header. Receivers accept only ES256 and only a kid present in the gateway JWKS; a kid starting with 'test-' is rejected unless allowTestKeys=true (CC-044); a kid starting with 'dev-' is rejected unless the devstack profile and allowTestKeys=true are both set (CC-137).

aud.description: Id of the receiving component: mcp-<system> or mcp-credential-broker. A single string, never an array.

prv.description: Revision of the policy data of the gateway (C7): a server that sees a revision newer than the one it holds refreshes its policy data at once. 0 means a gateway without policy data; receivers must not infer anything about policy from it (CC-068).

use.description: Purpose of the token (CC-249). call: a request of the MCP endpoint of a server or of the credential broker (user variant, or the service variant for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, ping and the broker GET /v1/systems). policy-data: the push of policy data to a server, POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data (C14). A receiver refuses a token whose purpose is not the one of the endpoint, whatever else is valid, so that a token minted for one purpose cannot be used for another.

UserClaims.description: Call on behalf of a user. The only variant accepted for tools/call and by the broker resolve and authenticator endpoints.

ServiceClaims.description: Gateway call without a user and without a session. Accepted only for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, ping (use call) and POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data (use policy-data) of a server, and GET /v1/systems of the broker (use call) (CC-069, CC-070, CC-249).

sub.description: sub from the IdP token (C1), unchanged.

grp.description: User groups from C9, only those with the mcp- prefix.

azp.description: OAuth client id of the AI client (C1).

tool.description: Server-side name of the tool being called. Present exactly for tools/call (and for the broker resolve and authenticator calls that serve it); absent for initialize, server/discover, subscriptions/listen, tools/list, and ping (CC-038, CC-069).

resource.description: URI of the resource being read (CC-260). Present exactly for resources/read (and for the broker resolve that serves it) and equal to params.uri; absent for every other request. At most one of tool and resource. Prompts have no claim: the gateway renders them itself (CC-259).

mfa.description: Seconds since the last authentication at an MFA acr level. Absent means unknown.

use.description: The user variant is only ever for calls (CC-249).

pty.description: Type of the principal (CC-260): agent (an autonomous agent, a service account of the IdP) or delegated (an agent acting for a person, defined now and not emitted before stage T2). Absent means a human; absent is the only form of a human, user is invalid.

act.description: The actor of a delegated call (CC-260, RFC 8693 actor): present exactly when pty is delegated. sub and azp identify the agent.

UserBase.description: Claims shared by the user variant for every receiver (CC-038, CC-069).

AdapterUserClaims.description: User variant for a receiver that is the sidecar of an adapter (CC-226, CC-193): the claims of UserClaims plus the classification of the administrator from the registry, as mcp_risk and mcp_action. Both come together, only with tool (a tools/call), and must fit each other (read for READ_ONLY, update or admin for UPDATE, delete or admin for DESTRUCTIVE). The gateway sends them only to a server that its configuration puts in adapter mode; the schema cannot tell the receiver, so the rule of the receiver is normative: a receiver that is not the sidecar of an adapter (a native server, the credential broker) rejects a token that carries mcp_risk or mcp_action as invalid_claims. The names are not act (RFC 8693, actor) on purpose.
